correctness.rationale: A common length-3 deletion output exists iff the intersection sum_i min(x_i,y_i) is >=3. Distinct valid codewords cannot share a coordinate of multiplicity >=3, hence at most four heavy codewords. Light multiplicities <=2 total at most 8: none for n>=9. Two light vectors of length n>=6 have intersection >=2n-8>=4, so at most one joins the heavy words. At n=5, the only light profiles are permutations of (0,1,2,2) and (2,1,1,1); the latter has no light neighbors, while any light A word has precisely two mutually incompatible light neighbors. Thus <=2 light words. Explicit four constant-vector codes plus the designated two or one light vectors reach all upper bounds. Independent enumeration finds light counts 16,10,4,1,0 and compatible-light pairs 12,0,0,0,0 for n=5..9; the all-length proof is symbolic, not an inference from those enumerations.

value.rationale: The natural next alphabet after the exact ternary three-survivor problem has a genuinely different exceptional compatibility graph, allowing exactly two light words at n=5; the theorem gives a sharp all-length classification of maximum code size including two finite thresholds. The intrinsic deletion-correction capacity and its nontrivial small-alphabet transition are independently useful, not a renamed bound or a mere finite table.

final_claim: For every n>=5, the largest 4-symbol unordered multiset code correcting n-3 deletions has size 6 at n=5, 5 at n=6..8, and 4 at n>=9.
limitations: Only unordered multisets over four symbols, three remaining symbols, and n>=5; no full isomorphism classification of optimal codes.
